chief_complaint: Management of hypertension, obesity, and sleep apnea (cardiometabolic risk)

Obstructive sleep apnea was identified in late 2014 and remains untreated. Recent visits have been predominantly wellness encounters, with two inpatient admissions of unspecified cause. Socially, the patient reports limited social contact despite full‑time employment and higher education. No recent laboratory data (lipids, glucose, renal function) are available, limiting full risk assessment.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include dental filling loss and gingivitis (2019), prior unemployment and related stress (2017‑2019), reports of environmental violence (2018), and earlier periods of full‑time employment and medication review due (2017‑2018). These reflect past psychosocial stressors and minor dental issues but no chronic organ disease.
social_determinants: Full‑time employment, higher education, limited social contact, stable socioeconomic status in Westfield, MA.

Charlson comorbidity index 0, clinical complexity moderate, polypharmacy risk low. clinical_impression: The patient presents with a moderate‑complexity cardiometabolic profile driven by obesity, borderline‑controlled hypertension, and untreated obstructive sleep apnea, placing him at elevated cardiovascular risk. Psychosocial isolation may further impede disease management. Absence of key laboratory and lifestyle data limits precise risk stratification, highlighting the need for comprehensive metabolic work‑up and initiation of sleep‑apnea therapy.
